security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives from inline parameters, fenced examples, and links. Confirmed risks are the intended RunComfy CLI execution, npm or npx installation guidance, and outbound RunComfy API submission and download behavior. No prompt injection attempt or hidden malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External command execution through RunComfy CLI
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running installation, login, generation, or download commands. Keep command arguments structured and avoid shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Global npm and npx installation guidance
remediation.suggestion: Pin the RunComfy CLI version in examples and prefer local project installation when possible. Tell users that global installs run third-party package code.
Clearly disclose that prompts, audio URLs, and generated outputs pass through RunComfy domains. Ask before sending sensitive or private media.
Document token scope, rotation, and storage expectations. Recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN only in controlled CI environments and avoid logging it.

content.value_statement: Creating short AI video clips usually requires model-specific parameters and service setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use Wan 2.7 on RunComfy with clear inputs and limits.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose Wan 2.7 instead of related video models.
Documents prompt, audio_url, aspect ratio, resolution, duration, negative prompt, and seed inputs.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for basic generation, lip-sync, and literal prompt control.
Describes audio requirements for lip-sync clips, including format, length, and size limits.
Lists expected exit codes and troubleshooting reference points for RunComfy CLI runs.
Summarizes security and privacy boundaries for tokens, outbound domains, and downloads.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account and the RunComfy CLI.
Sends prompts and media references to the external RunComfy model API.
Supports clips up to 15 seconds and up to 1080p resolution.
Does not generate voice internally; supplied audio drives lip-sync behavior.

use_cases.title: Product Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Create short product shots with controlled camera motion, lighting, and aspect ratio settings.

use_cases.title: Localized Spokesperson Clips
use_cases.description: Use one visual prompt with different audio tracks to create language-specific lip-sync variants.

use_cases.title: Video Model Routing
use_cases.description: Decide when Wan 2.7 is the right model compared with Seedance, Kling, HappyHorse, or LTX.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Text-to-Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple short clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wan 2.7 on RunComfy to create a five-second 1080p horizontal video of a product on a clean studio surface. Include camera movement, lighting, and one clear action.

prompt_templates.title: Vertical Social Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Specify format and motion for a platform-native short.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 Wan 2.7 prompt for a short cafe scene. Make the action simple, describe the camera movement, and include a negative prompt for flicker, subtitles, and watermarks.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Sync With Supplied Audio
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an external audio track to drive a spokesperson clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Wan 2.7 RunComfy request for a 12-second lip-synced spokesperson video. Use my audio URL, match the duration, and describe a locked camera with warm studio lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Variant Planning
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan controlled iterations across model settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three Wan 2.7 video variants for the same product prompt. Keep the seed stable for two variants, change one camera movement, and explain when prompt expansion should be disabled.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second product showcase video with a slow push-in and clean studio lighting.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects Wan 2.7, keeps the clip horizontal at 1080p, writes a concise motion-focused prompt, and recommends a targeted negative prompt.

output_examples.input: Make a vertical spokesperson clip that follows my 12-second voiceover.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks that the audio length is within range, uses the supplied audio URL for lip-sync, and prepares a vertical RunComfy generation plan.

output_examples.input: I need strict brand wording and do not want the prompt expanded.
output_examples.output: The assistant disables prompt expansion, keeps the prompt literal, and adds only concrete quality exclusions such as no subtitles and no watermark.

best_practices: Describe one primary action per clip and put camera movement near the start.
Use concrete negative prompts for visible problems such as flicker, subtitles, or watermarking.
Confirm RunComfy commands before sending private prompts, audio URLs, or reference media.
anti_patterns: Combining many unrelated actions in one short clip.
Using vague exclusions such as bad lighting or poor quality.
Sending sensitive media URLs without checking sharing permissions and retention needs.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It guides short text-to-video generation with Wan 2.7 through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it support lip-sync?
faq.answer: Yes. Wan 2.7 can use a supplied audio_url to drive lip-sync for supported WAV or MP3 files.

faq.question: What clip length can I request?
faq.answer: The documented duration range is 2 to 15 seconds, with whole-second values.

faq.question: Can it create 4K video?
faq.answer: No. The documented resolution options are 720p and 1080p.

faq.question: Where does generation run?
faq.answer: Generation runs through RunComfy model API endpoints, not only on the local machine.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
